audit_findings.title: Long-term marketable securities appear omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: at least $301.061 million, computed as $380.105 million of June 2026 available-for-sale securities less the entire $79.044 million current-investments balance already included; at least $4.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation removes available-for-sale investment income from owner earnings but the bridge adds only cash and current investments, omitting the corresponding long-term investment principal.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s overall financial position remains strong given that aggregate cash, cash equivalents and investments is $613,747 at December 31, 2025, including $121,541 in trading securities discussed below.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge inconsistency, although the exact omitted amount still requires the current-versus-long-term investment classification. Even under the conservative assumption that every dollar of current investments is available-for-sale, at least $301.061 million is omitted. That equals about 25.6% of base equity value and would raise base value from $15.67 to approximately $19.68 per share, so it is material despite remaining below the $38.78 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $510.828 million total investment balance by current/noncurrent classification and by available-for-sale versus trading status, exclude restricted or liability-matched assets, and rerun every scenario and the buy-below price with the verified unencumbered available-for-sale amount.

audit_findings.title: Unrecognized multiemployer pension withdrawal claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.904 million to $35.413 million filed present value for a twenty-payment withdrawal; $47.812 million to $56.833 million for a mass-withdrawal perpetuity; probability-weighted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered withdrawal obligation would be an equity claim outside recurring owner earnings and therefore requires a probability-weighted deduction from the equity bridge or explicit scenario treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has been advised that its withdrawal liability would have been $ 102,800 , $ 97,500 and $ 102,200 if it had withdrawn from the Plan during 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: No withdrawal liability is presently recorded, participation is contractually required through September 2027, and the record does not establish that withdrawal or mass withdrawal will occur. The filed present-value estimates equal roughly 2.8%-4.8% of the $1.177 billion base equity value, but the probability, timing, post-2025 liability and potential amount above the estimates are unresolved. This is therefore a contingent possibility whose materiality cannot yet be established, not a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain an updated actuarial withdrawal estimate incorporating Special Financial Assistance, identify management's plans after the September 2027 contract expiration, assign documented probabilities to continued participation, ordinary withdrawal and mass withdrawal, and rerun the bridge using the resulting probability-weighted present value.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation assets and liabilities require exact symmetry
audit_findings.magnitude: $130.723 million of June 2026 trading securities; $135.399 million combined current deferred compensation and noncurrent deferred compensation-and-other-liabilities captions; net amount and tax mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Trading-portfolio gains and matching compensation expense must be removed symmetrically from owner earnings, while the trading assets and associated deferred-compensation and tax liabilities must receive symmetric bridge treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: All gains and losses and related investment income from these investments, which are recorded in other income, net, are equally offset by corresponding increases and decreases in the Company’s deferred compensation liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates an economic hedge but the supplied valuation does not show the asset-liability and income-expense reconciliation. The gross trading assets equal about 11.1% of base equity value, and 2025 trading gains and matching expenses were $16.351 million, about 22.2% of the $73.7 million owner-earnings anchor. Adding the assets without liabilities would overstate value; purging gains while retaining matching expense would understate owner earnings. The potential scale is material even though the direction and net correction remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace all $130.723 million of trading securities to the $13.734 million current and applicable portion of the $121.665 million noncurrent liability caption, isolate other liabilities, reconcile related deferred taxes, and rerun the historical owner-earnings series after removing both hedge gains and matching compensation expense consistently.

audit_findings.title: The seven-year plant expansion may be omitted or double-counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $75 million to $85 million total filed program cost, $18.2 million incurred through June 2026, leaving $56.8 million to $66.8 million before separating maintenance and growth components
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded near-term capital outlays reduce owner earnings or the equity bridge, while growth reinvestment already represented in the RONTA framework must not be deducted a second time; maintenance spending belongs in normalized owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Company management believes that the total cost of this expansion, including new machinery and equipment, some of which is normal and recurring replacements over the next seven years, food processing infrastructure, and raw materials warehousing will approximate $75,000 to $85,000.
audit_findings.explanation: The remaining disclosed spending equals approximately 77%-91% of the $73.7 million annual owner-earnings anchor and is concentrated in 2026 and early 2027, making the treatment reasonably capable of changing value. The record does not identify how much is maintenance, replacement, capacity or efficiency capital, so it cannot establish whether the current model omits required cash spending, double-counts growth investment, or contains both effects.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the project schedule by year and classify each expenditure as maintenance, replacement, capacity or efficiency capital; reconcile the $10.7 million incurred in 2025 and $18.2 million cumulative amount to the anchor and then rerun explicit near-term owner earnings and RONTA-based reinvestment without overlap.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a prior-period trade-promotion reserve release unless normalized
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.7 million pre-tax; approximately $1.968 million after the filed 27.1% effective tax rate; approximately $0.37 per share of base value if fully capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the prior-period reserve release increases the 2025 owner-earnings anchor and is propagated through forecast owner earnings and terminal value as though recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company identified changes in business conditions in each of the periods presented that changed Management’s estimated current and future liabilities for prior period obligations resulting in a reduction in accrued liabilities and an increase in net product sales of $2,700 and $5,665 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $2.7 million prior-period revenue benefit, while whether it was removed from the supplied anchor is unresolved. It is only 3.7% of the $73.7 million anchor. Using the filed tax rate and the base operating-value-to-anchor multiple, full removal would reduce base value by approximately $0.37 per share, or about 2.4% of the $15.67 base estimate, and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $38.78 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $2.7 million release was removed from 2025 owner earnings; if not, normalize it and comparable historical reserve true-ups, then rerun the scenarios as a control check.

audit_findings.title: The forecast may rely on a trade regime whose stated date had already passed
audit_findings.mechanism: Tariffs can change operating margins, sales volume, working capital and required sourcing or production capital; tariff refunds could provide a smaller positive cash effect.
audit_findings.evidence: If regulators decide to impose tariffs, if the outcome of negotiations of the USMCA (which expires at June 30, 2026) is adverse to our cross-border shipments, or other surcharges are levied by Canada and Mexico, on products that previously qualified under USMCA, the impact of tariffs on our cross-border shipments could be significant.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing substantially updates the dated warning: cross-border USMCA shipments remained tariff-free and tariff developments had a nominal first-half 2026 impact. It also reports a new 10% global tariff, unresolved retaliatory and sourcing effects, and up to $1.3 million of possible refunds. Because the adverse future cost is not quantified and the filing covers only through June 30 rather than the September 6 valuation date, this is a forward-looking monitoring item rather than a demonstrated error in current numbers.
audit_findings.action: Verify tariff rules and realized costs from July 1 through September 6, 2026, document any refunds received or receivable, and revise scenario margins, volumes and capital needs only when post-quarter evidence establishes a sustained effect.
